questions.prompt: What does ‘endemic’ mean, as in ‘the lion-tailed macaque is endemic to the Western Ghats’?
questions.explain: Endemic species live naturally in only one region.

questions.prompt: Using the field-guide key: an animal has a backbone, no feathers and no fur, and moist skin (not scaly). What is it?
questions.explain: Moist skin without scales points to an amphibian.
Its mass flowering turns the Nilgiri hills blue.

questions.prompt: Which are endemic to (or famous in) the Western Ghats? Choose all that apply.
questions.explain: Polar bears live in the Arctic; snow leopards in the high Himalaya.

questions.prompt: During the challenge, suppose a key led you to the wrong name. Describe how you would find your mistake.
questions.modelAnswer: Go back through the key step by step, re-reading the field notes at each question. Check which answer didn't match the description, for example saying ‘no’ to ‘Does it have a backbone?’ for a frog. Change that answer and follow the correct branch. It helps to write down each answer so you can retrace your path.
rubric: Retrace the key step by step
Compare each answer with the evidence
questions.explain: Criterion C: evaluate your own method.

questions.prompt: Why is the bracket fungus important in the forest?
options: It decomposes dead wood and recycles nutrients
questions.explain: Decomposers return nutrients to the soil.
Butterflies and earthworms have no backbone.

questions.text: A region with a very large number of species, many found nowhere else, is called a biodiversity ___.
questions.explain: The Western Ghats is one of the world's biodiversity hotspots.
